correlates.name: Hypertensive emergency
correlates.presentation: 52-year-old man who ran out of his blood-pressure pills 3 weeks ago: 1 day of headache, blurred vision and new confusion. BP 228/136 in both arms, HR 96. Fundi: flame-shaped retinal hemorrhages and blurred optic disc margins. Lungs clear, no murmur, equal pulses.
correlates.workup: Creatinine 2.4 mg/dL (1.0 last year); UA 2+ protein with RBCs; a few fragmented RBCs on smear; troponin normal; head CT no bleed; ECG: tall precordial QRS voltage with downsloping ST depression and T inversion in V5-V6.
correlates.management: ICU with an IV titratable agent (nicardipine, clevidipine, labetalol; nitroprusside an option); lower MAP no more than ~25% in the first hour, then toward 160/100 over 2-6 h; never normalize quickly; then oral regimen and adherence review.

correlates.name: Metabolic alkalosis from vomiting
correlates.presentation: 36-year-old woman who has vomited many times a day for 3 days with a stomach virus; light-headed on standing, leg cramps. BP 102/64 lying, 84/52 standing; HR 114; dry mucous membranes, flat neck veins. No diuretic or antacid use.
correlates.workup: ABG pH 7.50, HCO3- 37, PCO2 48 (0.6 x 13 predicts 47.8 - simple, compensated); Na+ 135, K+ 2.9, Cl- 84; urine Cl- 8 mEq/L (low despite a high urine Na+ from bicarbonaturia); renin and aldosterone high.
correlates.management: IV isotonic saline (the chloride-responsive kind) with KCl replacement; restoring volume removes the angiotensin II/aldosterone drive so the kidney can excrete the extra HCO3-; antiemetic and treat the cause.

correlates.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
correlates.presentation: 56-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes for 15 years; a viral illness brought fever, anorexia and vomiting and she cut back her insulin. Now short of breath with deep, fast breathing (RR 30), HR 118, BP 100/60, dry mucous membranes, poor skin turgor, diffuse abdominal tenderness.
correlates.workup: pH 7.07, PCO2 18, HCO3- 5 (1.2 rule predicts PCO2 17 - simple, compensated); Na+ 132, Cl- 94, K+ 5.9 - gap 33; glucose 650 mg/dL; serum osm ~305; urine glucose and ketones positive; beta-hydroxybutyrate high.
correlates.management: IV isotonic saline first; regular insulin infusion once K+ is above 3.3; add K+ to fluids when K+ falls below ~5.3 (total-body K+ is depleted); add dextrose at glucose ~250 and keep insulin running until the gap closes; treat the trigger.

correlates.name: Methanol or ethylene glycol poisoning
correlates.presentation: 45-year-old man with alcohol use disorder found confused in his garage beside an empty unlabeled jug, ~12 h after drinking from it. Deep, fast breathing (RR 28), HR 110, BP 130/80, afebrile, no tinnitus; says his vision is blurry. Glucose 92 on fingerstick.
correlates.workup: Na+ 140, Cl- 102, HCO3- 8 (gap 30), PCO2 21, pH 7.20; measured osm 330 vs calculated 290 (osmolar gap 40); ketones negative, lactate 2.8 - too small to explain the gap; aspirin level undetectable.
correlates.management: Fomepizole at once to block alcohol dehydrogenase (ethanol if unavailable); IV bicarbonate for severe acidemia; hemodialysis for severe acidosis, vision or kidney injury, or high levels; cofactors (folate; thiamine and pyridoxine).

correlates.name: Non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis from diarrhea
correlates.presentation: 29-year-old man back from a trip abroad with 6 days of 10-12 watery stools a day; weak and thirsty. BP 98/60, HR 112, RR 24, dry mucous membranes; abdomen soft. No vomiting, no new medicines.
correlates.workup: Na+ 138, Cl- 114, HCO3- 14 - gap 10 (normal); K+ 3.0; pH 7.32, PCO2 28 (fits 1.2 rule); urine pH 5.0; urine Na+ 12, K+ 30, Cl- 67 (Na+ + K+ - Cl- = -25: NH4+ excretion intact); BUN 34, creatinine 1.4.
correlates.management: IV isotonic fluid (lactated Ringer or saline) with K+ replacement; oral bicarbonate or citrate only if acidemia is severe; oral rehydration and treatment of the cause once stable.

correlates.name: Distal (type 1) renal tubular acidosis
correlates.presentation: 34-year-old woman with 2 years of gritty dry eyes and a dry mouth comes in with left flank pain spreading to the groin and 3 weeks of muscle weakness. BP 118/76, HR 88. Both parotid glands are enlarged; left costovertebral angle tenderness.
correlates.workup: Na+ 139, Cl- 115, HCO3- 15 - gap 9; K+ 2.7; urine pH 6.8 although blood pH is 7.30; urine Na+ + K+ - Cl- = +20 (positive: NH4+ excretion low); CT: bilateral calcium phosphate stones and medullary calcification; anti-Ro/La positive.
correlates.management: Oral alkali, ideally potassium citrate (corrects the acidemia, replaces K+ and raises urine citrate to prevent stones); replete severe hypokalemia before giving alkali; treat the underlying autoimmune disease.

correlates.name: Proximal (type 2) renal tubular acidosis
correlates.presentation: 67-year-old man started on acetazolamide for glaucoma 6 weeks ago now has tingling fingers, fatigue and mild nausea. BP 132/80, HR 80, RR 20; exam otherwise normal. No bone pain, no polyuria, no kidney disease history.
correlates.workup: Na+ 140, Cl- 113, HCO3- 16 - gap 11; K+ 3.3; urine pH 5.2 at steady state, rising above 7.5 with fractional HCO3- excretion >15% during an IV bicarbonate load; urine has no glucose (serum 94), no amino acids and normal phosphate.
correlates.management: Stop or replace the carbonic anhydrase inhibitor. When alkali is needed it takes large doses (10-15 mEq/kg/day) plus K+, because extra filtered HCO3- is simply wasted; a thiazide can help by mild volume contraction.

correlates.name: Type 4 renal tubular acidosis (hypoaldosteronism)
correlates.presentation: 68-year-old man with 15 years of type 2 diabetes, diabetic kidney disease and hypertension; routine labs show K+ 6.1 with a stable eGFR of 42; he feels well. BP 148/88, HR 72, trace ankle edema. Meds: metformin and amlodipine; no K+ supplements, no ACE inhibitor.
correlates.workup: Na+ 137, K+ 6.1, Cl- 112, HCO3- 18 - gap 7 (normal); creatinine 1.7 mg/dL, eGFR 42; urine pH 5.0; plasma renin and aldosterone both low; ECG: tall, narrow, peaked T waves with normal QRS.
correlates.management: Low-K+ diet; stop K+-raising drugs (NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, K+-sparing diuretics); loop or thiazide diuretic; K+ binder such as patiromer; fludrocortisone only if no hypertension or edema; oral bicarbonate if acidemic.

correlates.name: Chronic respiratory acidosis from CO2 retention
correlates.presentation: 60-year-old man with ALS diagnosed 2 years ago: months of morning headaches, broken sleep, daytime sleepiness and a weak cough; no change this week. RR 22 with shallow breaths, SpO2 89% on room air, neck muscles working, lungs clear, no wheeze, BMI 23.
correlates.workup: ABG pH 7.32, PCO2 62, HCO3- 31 - HCO3- up ~7 for a 22 mmHg PCO2 rise (~0.3 per mmHg); Cl- 96; urine NH4+ high; FVC 45% predicted; chest x-ray clear.
correlates.management: Nocturnal bilevel noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation; avoid opioids, benzodiazepines and high-flow O2 (target SpO2 88-92%); lower PCO2 gradually - fast correction leaves a post-hypercapnic metabolic alkalosis.

correlates.name: Salicylate poisoning
correlates.presentation: 38-year-old woman brought in 4 h after swallowing most of a bottle of her over-the-counter arthritis pills: ringing in both ears, nausea, vomiting and agitation. Temp 38.3 C, RR 32, HR 118, BP 124/78; sweating; lungs clear.
correlates.workup: pH 7.46, PCO2 22, HCO3- 15; Na+ 140, Cl- 105 - gap 20; PCO2 is well below the ~29 that compensation alone predicts (a second, primary respiratory disorder); osmolar gap normal; glucose 88; serum drug level 70 mg/dL.
correlates.management: Activated charcoal; IV sodium bicarbonate to alkalinize serum and urine (ion trapping, urine pH 7.5-8); replete K+; dextrose if confused; dialysis for high levels, severe acidemia or brain/lung injury; if intubated keep ventilation high.

correlates.name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension
correlates.presentation: 31-year-old woman with a year of worsening breathlessness and fatigue on exertion and two near-faints climbing stairs; her mother died at 40 of a similar illness. Never smoked, no heart or lung history. Loud P2, left parasternal lift, JVP 9 cm, mild ankle edema, lungs clear.
correlates.workup: ECG: right-axis deviation, tall R in V1; CXR: large central pulmonary arteries that taper fast toward the periphery; echo: dilated thick RV, normal LV; right heart cath: mPAP 48, wedge 9 mmHg; normal PFTs and V/Q scan.
correlates.management: Vasoreactivity test during right heart cath; pulmonary vasodilators (endothelin receptor antagonist, PDE-5 inhibitor, prostacyclin analog; high-dose CCB only if vasoreactive); diuretics and O2 as needed; lung transplant if refractory.

correlates.name: Goodpasture syndrome
correlates.presentation: 22-year-old man who smokes a pack a day: a week of coughing up blood and breathlessness, then 3 days of cola-colored urine and less of it. BP 158/94, RR 24, SpO2 90%, crackles in both lungs. No nasal or sinus symptoms, no rash, no joint pain.
correlates.workup: Hb 9.8; creatinine 4.2 (0.9 last month); urine RBC casts, 2+ protein; CXR bilateral airspace filling; serum IgG to the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen; kidney biopsy: crescents in most glomeruli, no granulomas; ANCA negative.
correlates.management: Plasmapheresis to strip the circulating antibody, together with high-dose glucocorticoids and cyclophosphamide to stop its production; stop smoking; dialysis if renal failure progresses.

correlates.name: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
correlates.presentation: 42-year-old man with 4 months of bloody nasal crusts, sinus pain and ear fullness that two antibiotic courses did not help; now coughing up blood with fevers and 5 kg weight loss. The bridge of his nose has sunk; both eyes red; BP 150/90.
correlates.workup: PR3-ANCA (c-ANCA) positive; CT chest: several nodules, some cavitating; urine RBC casts, creatinine 2.1; biopsy: necrotizing small-vessel vasculitis with poorly formed granulomas and irregular geographic necrosis; anti-GBM negative.
correlates.management: Induction with high-dose glucocorticoids plus rituximab or cyclophosphamide (plasmapheresis kept for severe lung bleeding or renal failure); maintenance with rituximab or azathioprine.

correlates.name: Idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis
correlates.presentation: 5-year-old girl with 8 months of on-and-off cough, blood-streaked sputum, tiredness, pallor and poor weight gain. HR 120, RR 30, SpO2 93%; pale conjunctivae; fine crackles at both bases. Normal BP; no blood in urine, no sinus disease, normal stools.
correlates.workup: Hb 7.9, MCV 64, low ferritin; CXR: diffuse bilateral infiltrates that come and go; BAL: Prussian-blue-positive macrophages; ANCA, anti-GBM, ANA negative; normal UA and creatinine; biopsy: alveolar blood, no vasculitis or capillaritis.
correlates.management: Exclude every other cause of alveolar bleeding first; systemic glucocorticoids for acute bleeds, then long-term immunosuppression (prednisone, azathioprine) to prevent recurrence; iron replacement and transfusion as needed.

correlates.name: Acute pulmonary embolism, hemodynamically stable
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old woman 6 days after a knee replacement: sudden breathlessness and sharp right chest pain on deep breaths; anxious. Temp 37.8 C, HR 112, RR 26, BP 132/80, SpO2 91% on room air; lungs mostly clear; left calf larger than right.
correlates.workup: ABG: PaO2 62, PaCO2 31, wide A-a gradient; ECG: sinus tachycardia with nonspecific ST-T changes; CT angiogram: filling defects in right lower-lobe segmental arteries; RV normal size; troponin normal.
correlates.management: Anticoagulate now - LMWH or a factor Xa inhibitor (rivaroxaban, apixaban) for at least 3 months; no thrombolysis while normotensive; IVC filter only if anticoagulation is contraindicated; image the legs for the source.

correlates.name: Massive pulmonary embolism
correlates.presentation: 66-year-old man on day 4 of a hospital stay for a hip fracture, no prophylaxis given, suddenly collapses gasping while straining on the commode. BP 72/40, HR 132, RR 34, SpO2 82% on 6 L; neck veins distended; cold, mottled legs; lungs clear; heart sounds normal.
correlates.workup: Too unstable for CT: bedside echo shows a dilated, hypokinetic RV pushing the septum into a small, underfilled LV and no pericardial fluid; troponin and BNP elevated; ECG sinus tachycardia with a new rightward axis.
correlates.management: Systemic thrombolysis (tPA) at the bedside unless contraindicated; surgical or catheter clot removal if lysis fails or is contraindicated; heparin; cautious fluid and norepinephrine for BP; never send an unstable patient to the scanner.

correlates.name: Pulmonary infarction
correlates.presentation: 71-year-old man with left heart failure (EF 25%), mostly in bed for 2 weeks, has 2 days of sharp right chest pain on breathing in, bright-red hemoptysis and a low fever. HR 104, RR 24, BP 118/74, SpO2 92%; a scratchy sound over the right lower chest; dull right base.
correlates.workup: CXR: pleural-based, wedge-shaped right lower-lobe opacity with its apex toward the hilum and a small effusion; CT angiogram: occluded subsegmental artery supplying that area; histology: hemorrhagic necrosis of alveolar walls.
correlates.management: Anticoagulate as for any lung-artery clot; analgesia for the pleuritic pain; optimize the heart failure (poor bronchial back-up flow let the tissue die); antibiotics only if the area becomes infected or cavitates.

correlates.name: Deep vein thrombosis
correlates.presentation: 63-year-old woman 8 days after a right hip replacement, sent home without prophylaxis: 2 days of aching, warm swelling of the right calf and thigh. Temp 37.6 C, HR 92, SpO2 98%, no chest pain or breathlessness. Right calf 4 cm larger than the left, with pitting edema.
correlates.workup: Compression ultrasound (test of choice): right popliteal and femoral segments do not collapse under the probe and hold echogenic clot with no Doppler flow; contrast venography (gold standard) not needed; platelets and creatinine normal.
correlates.management: Anticoagulate - LMWH or apixaban/rivaroxaban for 3 months for a provoked clot; early walking; IVC filter only if anticoagulation is impossible; consider looking for silent clot in the lungs; prophylaxis after future surgery.

correlates.name: Trousseau syndrome (malignancy-associated thrombosis)
correlates.presentation: 64-year-old smoker with 10 kg weight loss over 3 months and upper-abdominal pain into the back. Over 4 weeks, tender red cords have appeared on the left forearm, then the right thigh, then the chest wall, each fading as the next appears. No surgery, travel or family history.
correlates.workup: Duplex: superficial vein clots at each site plus a fresh left popliteal clot; platelets and coagulation tests normal; thrombophilia panel unrevealing; CA 19-9 high; CT abdomen: 3-cm mass in the body of the pancreas.
correlates.management: Anticoagulate with LMWH or a factor Xa inhibitor (warfarin often fails here) for as long as the cancer is active; stage and treat the tumor; any unprovoked clot earns age-appropriate cancer screening and imaging.

correlates.name: Factor V Leiden
correlates.presentation: 24-year-old woman 4 months into an estrogen-containing pill: painful, swollen right calf after a 9-hour flight. Her father had a leg clot at 35 and an aunt had a lung clot after childbirth. HR 90, SpO2 99%; right calf 3 cm larger and tender.
correlates.workup: Ultrasound: right popliteal clot; antithrombin, protein C and protein S levels normal; clotting time fails to lengthen normally when activated protein C is added.
correlates.management: Anticoagulate 3-6 months (apixaban, rivaroxaban or LMWH); stop estrogen for good - progestin-only or nonhormonal contraception; no lifelong therapy after one provoked clot; prophylaxis around future surgery, pregnancy and postpartum.

correlates.name: Post-thrombotic syndrome
correlates.presentation: 55-year-old man treated for a left femoral-popliteal clot 4 years ago: the left leg now swells, aches and feels heavy by evening and improves with elevation. Brown skin and hard, thickened tissue above the inner ankle, with a shallow weeping ulcer there; varicosities.
correlates.workup: Duplex: thickened, partly recanalized femoral and popliteal veins with reflux >1 s on standing (incompetent valves) and no fresh clot; ankle-brachial index 1.05 (arterial supply normal).
correlates.management: Graded compression stockings or multilayer bandages and leg elevation; ulcer wound care (hyperbaric therapy in selected cases); walking program; vascular surgery referral for the obstructed or refluxing segment.

correlates.name: Cholesterol gallstones
correlates.presentation: 41-year-old woman, BMI 34, who lost 12 kg on a very-low-calorie diet this year: 4 episodes in 2 months of steady right upper-abdominal pain 1-2 h after fatty meals, lasting 2-3 h, with nausea, spreading to the right shoulder blade. Afebrile, mild RUQ tenderness, no jaundice.
correlates.workup: Ultrasound: several mobile echogenic foci in the gallbladder casting acoustic shadows; normal wall; bile duct not dilated; LFTs, lipase and WBC normal. Stones are yellow - bile held more sterol than its bile salts and lecithin could carry.
correlates.management: Elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic stones; smaller low-fat meals meanwhile; ursodeoxycholic acid only for poor surgical candidates; note fibrates add the same risk by cutting bile acid synthesis.

correlates.name: Abetalipoproteinemia
correlates.presentation: 10-year-old boy with greasy, bulky, foul stools and poor growth since infancy now walks unsteadily on a wide base, has lost his ankle reflexes and his position and vibration sense, and cannot see well at dusk. Height and weight below the 3rd percentile; parents are first cousins.
correlates.workup: Total cholesterol 40, TG 10 mg/dL; no apoB-48 or apoB-100 - chylomicrons, VLDL, IDL and LDL all absent; smear: RBCs with irregular thorny projections; vitamin E very low, INR 1.6; duodenal biopsy: lipid-stuffed enterocytes.
correlates.management: Restrict long-chain fat and use medium-chain triglycerides (absorbed straight into portal blood); high-dose fat-soluble vitamins - vitamin E above all, plus A, D and K - to halt the nerve and retinal damage.

correlates.name: Niemann-Pick disease type C
correlates.presentation: 9-year-old girl, normal until age 7, with 2 years of clumsiness, falling grades and slurred speech, plus spells of sudden limpness when she laughs. She cannot move her eyes up or down on command, though side-to-side gaze is full. Spleen palpable 3 cm below the costal margin.
correlates.workup: Lipid panel unremarkable; cultured skin fibroblasts: unesterified cholesterol trapped in lysosomes, bright on filipin staining; plasma oxysterols high; MRI: cerebellar atrophy.
correlates.management: No cure: miglustat (substrate reduction) can slow neurologic decline; supportive care - antiseizure drugs, physical, speech and feeding therapy; genetic counseling (autosomal recessive).

correlates.name: Tangier disease
correlates.presentation: 38-year-old man with 3 years of numbness and weakness of both hands and loss of pain and temperature sense over the arms and face; spleen tip palpable; no proteinuria or anemia. His brother had a heart attack at 42.
correlates.workup: HDL 2 mg/dL with apoA-I nearly absent; LDL 60, TG 210 mg/dL; rectal or tonsil biopsy: cholesteryl ester-filled macrophages; his cells cannot move cholesterol to the outer membrane leaflet for loading onto HDL.
correlates.management: No specific therapy: low-fat diet, manage atherosclerotic risk (statin if warranted), supportive neuropathy care; splenectomy or tonsillectomy only for symptoms. Raising HDL with drugs does not help.

correlates.name: Elevated lipoprotein(a)
correlates.presentation: 44-year-old man, nonsmoker, BP 118/76, BMI 24, no diabetes, exercises daily and eats little saturated fat, has an MI; a standard lipid panel last year was unremarkable. His father and paternal uncle had MIs in their 40s. No tendon nodules or corneal rings.
correlates.workup: LDL 128, HDL 52, TG 110 mg/dL; TSH, glucose and A1c normal; a separate assay finds 210 nmol/L (high >125) of an LDL-like particle carrying an extra plasminogen-like glycoprotein; the level is genetically set and barely moves with diet.
correlates.management: Aggressive LDL lowering (high-intensity statin, then a PCSK9 inhibitor, which also cuts Lp(a) ~25%); niacin lowers Lp(a) but has not cut events; avoid trans fats; test first-degree relatives.

correlates.name: Familial chylomicronemia (type I)
correlates.presentation: 7-year-old boy with his third bout of severe upper-abdominal pain and vomiting since age 3, each after a fatty meal; his sister has had similar attacks. Small yellow papules with red rims on the buttocks and elbows; liver and spleen enlarged. Lean, no diabetes; parents healthy.
correlates.workup: Lipase 1,100; TG 3,200 mg/dL; plasma left in the fridge overnight forms a creamy top layer over a clear bottom layer; LDL and HDL low; post-heparin lipoprotein lipase activity absent (or apoC-II missing); no early coronary disease in kin.
correlates.management: Very-low-fat diet (under 15-20% of calories) with medium-chain triglyceride oil; no alcohol or estrogen; fibrates, statins and omega-3s work poorly because the clearing enzyme is missing; treat pancreatitis episodes supportively.

correlates.name: Familial hypercholesterolemia
correlates.presentation: 19-year-old man with 2 months of chest tightness when he runs; firm, painless nodules thicken both Achilles tendons. Father died of an MI at 41, grandfather at 50; his 14-year-old sister already takes a cholesterol pill. Nonsmoker, BMI 23, BP 118/72.
correlates.workup: Total cholesterol 325, LDL 250, HDL 45, TG 110 mg/dL; TSH, glucose, creatinine and urine protein normal; genetic test: loss-of-function LDL receptor mutation (or defective apoB-100, or gain-of-function PCSK9); homozygotes run LDL >500.
correlates.management: High-intensity statin plus diet; add ezetimibe, then a PCSK9 inhibitor if LDL stays high on maximal statin; homozygotes add lomitapide, evinacumab or LDL apheresis; screen relatives - affected children may start a statin at ~10.

correlates.name: Familial dysbetalipoproteinemia (type III)
correlates.presentation: 52-year-old man, BMI 31, type 2 diabetes diagnosed last year, coronary stent at 48; now calf pain after walking 2 blocks. Firm, bumpy yellow plaques over both elbows and knees; Achilles tendons normal. A screening panel showed cholesterol and triglycerides both near 400.
correlates.workup: Total cholesterol 390 and TG 420 mg/dL - raised about equally; VLDL is unusually cholesterol-rich, with chylomicron remnants and IDL accumulating; LDL not high; apoE genotype E2/E2; TSH normal.
correlates.management: Treat triggers (weight, diabetes, hypothyroidism, alcohol); diet; statin and/or fibrate, to which it responds very well; aggressive vascular risk reduction because coronary and peripheral artery disease come early.

correlates.name: Familial hypertriglyceridemia (type IV)
correlates.presentation: 38-year-old man with no symptoms whose fasting TG has run 350-500 mg/dL on several checks while LDL stayed normal; his mother and brother have the same pattern. BMI 27, waist 94 cm, BP 124/78; no skin or tendon deposits, no abdominal pain; 2 beers a week.
correlates.workup: Fasting TG 480 mg/dL from excess VLDL; LDL 105, HDL 42; fasting glucose 96, A1c 5.6%; TSH, creatinine and urine protein normal; refrigerated serum evenly cloudy with no creamy top layer; same pattern in first-degree relatives.
correlates.management: Lifestyle first - weight loss, less refined carbohydrate, sugar and alcohol, regular exercise; rule out secondary causes; fibrate or prescription omega-3 once TG is 500 or more to prevent pancreatitis; statin for overall ASCVD risk.

correlates.name: Hypoalphalipoproteinemia
correlates.presentation: 41-year-old man, nonsmoker, BP 120/76, BMI 24, no diabetes, active, has exertional chest pressure and an abnormal stress test; his HDL has never been above 20 mg/dL. Brother had bypass surgery at 45. Exam normal - no corneal clouding, no neuropathy, spleen not felt.
correlates.workup: HDL 18 mg/dL with low apoA-I from accelerated apoA-I/A-II breakdown; LDL 110 and TG 120 mg/dL; esterified cholesterol fraction normal; no anemia or proteinuria; TSH normal; no anabolic steroid use.
correlates.management: No proven HDL-raising therapy: treat overall risk - high-intensity statin for LDL, aspirin for established coronary disease, exercise, no smoking; niacin and CETP inhibitors raise HDL without reducing events.

correlates.name: Wolman disease
correlates.presentation: 6-week-old girl with persistent vomiting, watery fatty stools and poor weight gain since 2 weeks of age; abdomen hugely distended by a firm liver and spleen; low-grade fevers; pale; now below her birth weight.
correlates.workup: Abdominal x-ray: both adrenal glands enlarged with dense speckled calcification; AST/ALT mildly high; anemia; lipid-filled vacuoles in lymphocytes and foam cells in marrow; lysosomal acid lipase activity absent in leukocytes.
correlates.management: Enzyme replacement with sebelipase alfa (recombinant lysosomal acid lipase) as early as possible; nutritional support; stem cell transplant in some; untreated, death usually comes within the first year.

correlates.name: LCAT deficiency
correlates.presentation: 34-year-old woman whose vision has slowly clouded; both corneas show a diffuse grayish haze, densest at the rims. A year of fatigue, pallor, frothy urine and ankle swelling. BP 146/92. Two siblings have the same eye change; no neuropathy, spleen not enlarged.
correlates.workup: HDL 8 mg/dL; plasma cholesterol mostly unesterified (ester fraction <10%); normocytic anemia with target cells; urine protein 3 g/day, creatinine 1.6; kidney biopsy: lipid deposits and foam cells in the glomeruli.
correlates.management: No approved specific therapy: low-fat diet, ACE inhibitor or ARB to slow proteinuric kidney disease, dialysis or kidney transplant for renal failure, corneal transplant for severe clouding; manage cardiovascular risk.

correlates.name: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease
correlates.presentation: 49-year-old woman, BMI 36, with type 2 diabetes and hypertension, has fatigue and a dull ache under the right ribs. Drinks less than 1 drink a week; no hepatitis risk factors; no jaundice or confusion. A smooth, slightly enlarged hepatic edge is felt 3 cm below the costal margin.
correlates.workup: ALT 82, AST 54 (ALT > AST); alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin normal; hepatitis B and C negative; ultrasound: diffusely bright, echogenic hepatic parenchyma; biopsy: large triglyceride droplets pushing hepatocyte nuclei aside.
correlates.management: Gradual 7-10% weight loss with diet and exercise; control diabetes (GLP-1 agonist or pioglitazone help), lipids and BP; avoid alcohol; vaccinate against hepatitis A and B; stage fibrosis (FIB-4, elastography).

correlates.name: Metabolic syndrome
correlates.presentation: 52-year-old man, sedentary office worker with no diabetes history, in for a check-up. Waist 107 cm (42 in), BMI 31, BP 136/86 on two visits; dark, velvety skin on the back of the neck. His father has type 2 diabetes.
correlates.workup: Fasting glucose 108 mg/dL, A1c 5.9%, fasting insulin high; TG 190, HDL 36, LDL 128 mg/dL; ALT, TSH and urine albumin normal.
correlates.management: Lifestyle first: 7-10% weight loss, 150+ min/week of moderate exercise, DASH or Mediterranean pattern low in refined carbohydrate and added sugar; then treat each component (statin, antihypertensive, metformin if glucose progresses).

correlates.name: Diabetic dyslipidemia
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old man with type 2 diabetes for 8 years, poorly controlled (A1c 9.6%), BMI 33, inactive, eats large carbohydrate-heavy meals; no symptoms, here for annual labs. BP 128/78; no skin or tendon deposits; thyroid normal; his siblings have normal lipids.
correlates.workup: Fasting TG 340, HDL 31, LDL 152 mg/dL with many small dense LDL particles; apoB high; glucose 214; TSH, creatinine and urine albumin normal. Insulin resistance drives hepatic VLDL overproduction while lipoprotein lipase activity falls.
correlates.management: Moderate- to high-intensity statin (all patients with diabetes aged 40-75); tighten glucose control, which itself lowers TG; weight loss, exercise, less refined carbohydrate and alcohol; fibrate or omega-3 only if TG stays >=500.

correlates.name: Dyslipidemia secondary to hypothyroidism
correlates.presentation: 46-year-old woman with 6 months of fatigue, 6 kg weight gain, constipation, feeling cold, dry skin and heavier periods. Puffy face, HR 54, ankle reflexes relax slowly after the tap; firm, nontender, enlarged thyroid. Her LDL was normal 2 years ago.
correlates.workup: LDL 205 mg/dL (110 two years ago), IDL increased, TG mildly up (190), HDL normal; TSH 22 mU/L, low free T4, anti-TPO positive; CK mildly high (650). Fewer hepatic LDL receptors explain the rise.
correlates.management: Levothyroxine first, then recheck lipids in 6-8 weeks - LDL usually falls back toward baseline; add a statin only if it stays high, since statins started in an untreated low-thyroid state carry more muscle toxicity.

correlates.name: Dyslipidemia secondary to nephrotic syndrome
correlates.presentation: 34-year-old man with 6 weeks of puffy eyes each morning, swollen legs by evening, foamy urine and 5 kg weight gain. BP 132/84; pitting edema to the knees; no rash, joint pain or visible blood in the urine.
correlates.workup: Albumin 1.9 g/dL; urine protein 7.5 g/day with oval fat bodies, no RBC casts; total cholesterol 380, LDL 270, TG 320, HDL 38 mg/dL (low oncotic pressure drives hepatic VLDL/apoB output); TSH normal; biopsy: podocyte foot-process effacement.
correlates.management: Treat the glomerular disease (e.g. glucocorticoids); ACE inhibitor or ARB to cut protein loss; salt restriction and a loop diuretic for edema; statin if lipids stay high; consider anticoagulation when albumin is very low.

correlates.name: Hypertriglyceridemia-induced acute pancreatitis
correlates.presentation: 45-year-old man with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes (A1c 11%) and BMI 34 who rarely drinks: 10 h of severe, constant upper-abdominal pain into the back with vomiting, worse lying flat. Temp 37.9 C, HR 118, BP 108/66; epigastric tenderness and guarding.
correlates.workup: Lipase 1,400 U/L (>3x upper limit); TG 2,400 mg/dL in a milky sample; glucose 380, A1c 11%; lipoprotein lipase and apoC-II normal; calcium normal; ultrasound: no stones, normal bile duct; CT: swollen, edematous pancreas.
correlates.management: NPO, generous IV fluids, analgesia; IV insulin infusion (with dextrose) to drive lipoprotein lipase and drop TG fast, plasmapheresis if severe; then a fibrate, glucose control and no alcohol to keep TG well below 500 mg/dL.

correlates.name: Statin-associated myopathy / rhabdomyolysis
correlates.presentation: 67-year-old man on a top-dose cholesterol pill for 3 years started clarithromycin for pneumonia 5 days ago; drinks grapefruit juice daily. Now his thighs and shoulders ache and are weak - he can barely rise from a chair - and his urine is tea-colored. Proximal muscles tender.
correlates.workup: CK 18,500 U/L (>10x upper limit); urine dipstick strongly positive for blood but no RBCs on microscopy; creatinine 2.1 (0.9 baseline); K+ 5.4; AST/ALT mildly up; TSH normal.
correlates.management: Stop the cholesterol drug and clarithromycin; IV isotonic fluid for urine output ~200 mL/h; watch K+, Ca2+ and creatinine; after recovery retry a low-dose HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor not cleared by CYP3A4, or ezetimibe or bempedoic acid.

correlates.name: Familial combined hyperlipidemia
correlates.presentation: 47-year-old man who had an MI at 46; BMI 29, BP 136/86. No tendon nodules, no palm-crease or elbow deposits. His father had an MI at 52; one sister has only a high cholesterol, a brother only high triglycerides, and his own pattern has shifted between checks.
correlates.workup: Total cholesterol 310, LDL 190, TG 420 mg/dL - VLDL and LDL both up; apoB 160 mg/dL, disproportionately high; VLDL-to-TG ratio normal (not remnant disease); apoE E3/E3; TSH, glucose and urine protein normal.
correlates.management: Lifestyle (weight loss, less saturated fat, sugar and alcohol) plus a high-intensity statin for LDL/apoB; add ezetimibe if needed and a fibrate or omega-3 for TG >=500; treat BP and glucose; screen first-degree relatives.

correlates.name: Homocystinuria
correlates.presentation: 14-year-old boy, 188 cm with an arm span of 196 cm, a mild learning disability and worsening nearsightedness; both lenses are partly dislocated. Now a swollen, painful left calf after a 1-hour car ride. An uncle had a stroke at 30. Joints not hypermobile; no murmur.
correlates.workup: Plasma methionine 420 umol/L (normal <40) with low cystathionine and cystine; cystathionine beta-synthase activity low in cultured fibroblasts; ultrasound: left popliteal clot; echo: normal aortic root.
correlates.management: Trial of high-dose pyridoxine (vitamin B6) - about half respond; methionine-restricted, cysteine-supplemented diet; betaine; folate and B12; anticoagulate the clot and give prophylaxis around surgery and immobilization.

correlates.name: Embolic stroke from carotid atherosclerosis
correlates.presentation: 70-year-old former smoker with hypertension: 2 hours of slurred speech and weakness of the left arm and lower left face, still present on arrival. BP 176/94, HR 78 and regular; whooshing sounds heard over both sides of the neck; glucose 112.
correlates.workup: CT: no bleed; MRI: restricted diffusion in right MCA cortex; CT angiogram: 80% right ICA stenosis with an ulcerated plaque; ECG sinus rhythm. Plaque histology: thin fibrous cap, large lipid core, many macrophages, few smooth muscle cells.
correlates.management: IV alteplase or tenecteplase within 4.5 h if no bleed (BP <185/110 first); thrombectomy for a large-vessel occlusion; then antiplatelet, high-intensity statin, BP control and endarterectomy within ~2 weeks for symptomatic 70-99% stenosis.

correlates.name: Stable angina
correlates.presentation: 55-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes: 6 months of crushing midchest pressure that comes on climbing stairs, lasts about 7 minutes and goes away with rest; the pattern has not changed. Father had an MI at 50. BP 138/84, HR 76, normal exam at rest.
correlates.workup: Resting ECG normal; troponin normal; exercise ECG: 2 mm horizontal ST depression in V4-V6 at 7 minutes with his usual pain, resolving in recovery; angiography, if done: a fixed ~75% LAD narrowing.
correlates.management: SL nitroglycerin every 5 min up to 3 doses, then EMS; a beta-1-selective blocker first (no ISA agents such as acebutolol); add a CCB, long-acting nitrate or ranolazine; aspirin, high-intensity statin; revascularize if refractory.

correlates.name: Unstable angina
correlates.presentation: 47-year-old smoker with diabetes and a strong family history: chest pain that used to come only when jogging now comes after one flight of stairs, and today came on walking to the car and lasted 20 minutes at rest; SL nitroglycerin barely helps. BP 146/90, HR 96; exam normal.
correlates.workup: ECG during pain: 1.5 mm ST depression and T-wave inversion in V4-V6; high-sensitivity troponin normal on arrival and again 4-6 h later; CK-MB normal - no myocyte death.
correlates.management: Aspirin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor, heparin, beta blocker, nitrates, high-intensity statin, ACE inhibitor; no fibrinolysis; urgent angiography/PCI within 24-48 h, emergent if pain persists or shock, heart failure or sustained VT appear.

correlates.name: Vasospastic angina
correlates.presentation: 38-year-old woman who smokes and takes sumatriptan for migraines: 3 weeks of crushing chest pain that wakes her near 5 a.m. and lasts 10-15 minutes; she jogs daily without any pain. Her fingers turn white, then blue, in the cold. Normal exam between attacks.
correlates.workup: ECG in an episode: 3 mm ST elevation in II, III, aVF that resolves within minutes of SL nitroglycerin; troponin normal twice; angiography: no fixed narrowing, but IV acetylcholine provokes a reversible focal narrowing of the right coronary.
correlates.management: Calcium channel blocker first line (diltiazem, verapamil or a dihydropyridine); SL nitroglycerin for attacks, long-acting nitrate if needed; stop smoking and triggers (triptans, cocaine, alcohol); avoid beta blockers (unopposed alpha tone).

correlates.name: NSTEMI
correlates.presentation: 66-year-old woman with diabetes and CKD: 3 hours of pressure in the chest and jaw at rest with nausea and sweating, not relieved by 2 SL nitroglycerin. BP 150/88, HR 104, SpO2 96%, lungs clear, no murmur.
correlates.workup: ECG: 2 mm horizontal ST depression in V3-V6 and T inversion in I and aVL, no ST elevation, no new bundle branch block; troponin I 0.9 ng/mL on arrival rising to 3.4 at 4 h; CK-MB up; echo: lateral hypokinesis.
correlates.management: Aspirin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor, heparin, beta blocker, nitrates, high-intensity statin, ACE inhibitor; never fibrinolysis; urgent angiography/PCI in 24-48 h - immediate if shock, refractory pain, new MR or septal defect, or sustained VT.

correlates.name: STEMI
correlates.presentation: 47-year-old man with hypertension and high cholesterol: 30 minutes of constant, squeezing 10/10 substernal pain at rest spreading to the left shoulder, unrelieved by SL nitroglycerin in the ambulance; sweating heavily. HR 108, BP 104/68, SpO2 95%, lungs clear.
correlates.workup: ECG: 3 mm ST elevation in I and aVL with reciprocal ST depression in III and aVF; troponin and CK-MB rising; bedside echo: lateral wall not moving; cath: abrupt complete cutoff of the left circumflex.
correlates.management: Chewed aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitor, heparin, nitrates if BP allows; emergent PCI, door-to-balloon <=90 min; if PCI is >120 min away, fibrinolysis within 30 min of first contact, then transfer; high-intensity statin; beta blocker within 24 h.

correlates.name: Ventricular fibrillation early after MI
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old man 40 minutes into crushing chest pain from an inferior MI, waiting for transfer, suddenly slumps unresponsive with gasping breaths that then stop. No carotid or femoral pulse, BP unrecordable, skin gray.
correlates.workup: Monitor: rapid, chaotic undulations of varying size and shape with no identifiable QRS complexes, P waves or T waves; no pulse. Mechanism: reentry in ischemic, electrically unstable muscle - the most common complication of the first 24 h.
correlates.management: Immediate CPR and unsynchronized defibrillation (biphasic 120-200 J), CPR for 2 min between shocks; epinephrine every 3-5 min; amiodarone or lidocaine if shocks fail; then emergent reperfusion of the culprit artery.

correlates.name: Early post-MI fibrinous pericarditis
correlates.presentation: 64-year-old man on day 2 after a large anterior STEMI reperfused late: new sharp chest pain, different from his infarct pain, that is worse with deep breaths. Temp 37.8 C, HR 92, BP 124/76; a scratchy, three-part sound at the left sternal border; lungs clear.
correlates.workup: ECG: anterior ST elevation persists, plus new mild ST elevation and PR depression outside that territory; troponin falling, CK-MB not re-elevated; echo: thin rim of pericardial fluid, no chamber collapse; histology: neutrophils and fibrin.
correlates.management: Usually settles within days; high-dose aspirin for pain (preferred over other NSAIDs and steroids, which can impair scar healing this early); colchicine may be added; reassess any anticoagulant if the effusion grows.

correlates.name: Dressler syndrome
correlates.presentation: 47-year-old man 2 months after a stent for a lateral STEMI, on dual antiplatelet therapy: 4 days of chest pain worse on breathing in, with low-grade fevers and malaise. Temp 38.3 C, HR 98, BP 128/80; scratchy sound over the lower sternum; lungs clear, no edema.
correlates.workup: WBC 13,200; ESR 70 mm/h, CRP high; ECG: diffuse concave ST elevation in nearly all leads with PR depression and no reciprocal change, plus old Q waves in I and aVL from the prior infarct; CK-MB normal; echo: small effusion, EF unchanged.
correlates.management: Anti-inflammatory therapy - high-dose aspirin (the NSAID of choice after MI) or colchicine, which also cuts recurrence; glucocorticoids only if refractory; continue antiplatelet therapy; follow the effusion.

correlates.name: Ventricular free wall rupture
correlates.presentation: 76-year-old woman with hypertension, day 5 after her first MI - a large anterior STEMI never reperfused: brief new chest pain, then sudden collapse. Neck veins distended, heart sounds faint, BP 60 by palpation, then no pulse while the monitor shows an organized rhythm.
correlates.workup: Monitor: organized narrow-complex rhythm with no pulse (PEA); bedside echo: large pericardial collection containing clot, with right atrium and ventricle collapsing in diastole; diastolic pressures equal in all four chambers; no new murmur.
correlates.management: Emergency surgical repair of the myocardial tear; pericardiocentesis only as a bridge; IV fluids; stop anticoagulants. Few survive, so prevention by early reperfusion matters most.

correlates.name: Left ventricular pseudoaneurysm
correlates.presentation: 68-year-old man 10 days after an inferolateral MI that was reperfused late: vague chest discomfort and breathlessness. BP 112/70, HR 90; a new to-and-fro murmur at the apex; neck veins normal; no fever, no positional chest pain.
correlates.workup: Echo/cardiac MRI: a sac off the inferolateral wall joined to the LV by a narrow neck (much smaller than the sac's diameter); its wall is pericardium and organized clot with no myocardium; Doppler flow in during systole, out in diastole.
correlates.management: Urgent surgical repair even if symptoms are mild - this is a contained tear that can rupture completely at any time; control BP meanwhile and avoid anticoagulation where possible.

correlates.name: True left ventricular aneurysm
correlates.presentation: 62-year-old man 6 months after a large anterior-apical MI: months of exertional breathlessness and palpitations; today sudden right-sided weakness and inability to speak. Broad apical impulse displaced laterally that pushes outward in systole; S3; no neck bruits; BP 128/76.
correlates.workup: ECG: Q waves with ST elevation in V1-V4 still present 6 months after the MI; echo: thin, wide-necked apical segment of scarred myocardium bulging outward in systole, lined by a layered mural thrombus; no communication with the pericardium.
correlates.management: Anticoagulation (warfarin) for the mural thrombus; full HFrEF therapy; ICD or ablation for recurrent VT; surgical resection of the scarred segment only for refractory heart failure or VT - rupture is rare.

correlates.name: Papillary muscle rupture
correlates.presentation: 71-year-old man on day 4 after an inferior STEMI: sudden severe breathlessness, pink frothy sputum, cannot lie flat. BP 86/54, HR 124, RR 34, SpO2 84%; crackles to both apices; a new holosystolic apical murmur radiating to the axilla, which may be soft; no thrill.
correlates.workup: Echo: flail posterior mitral leaflet with a torn chordal head whipping into the left atrium and severe eccentric regurgitation; hyperdynamic LV; PCWP 32 mmHg with giant v waves; no O2 step-up from RA to RV; CXR: bilateral alveolar edema.
correlates.management: Afterload reduction (IV nitroprusside), intra-aortic balloon pump or other mechanical support, diuretics and ventilation as a bridge to emergent mitral valve repair or replacement, with coronary revascularization at the same time.

correlates.name: Ventricular septal rupture
correlates.presentation: 69-year-old woman on day 4 after an anterior STEMI from an LAD occlusion: sudden breathlessness and low BP. BP 84/50, HR 118; new loud, harsh holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border with a palpable thrill; JVP 12 cm, tender enlarged liver, pedal edema.
correlates.workup: Right heart cath: O2 saturation 62% in the right atrium jumping to 84% in the RV and pulmonary artery (left-to-right shunt, Qp:Qs 3:1); color Doppler: jet through a defect in the apical septum; mitral valve competent.
correlates.management: Afterload reduction and inotropes, intra-aortic balloon pump or other mechanical support as a bridge to urgent surgical (or transcatheter) closure of the defect, plus revascularization; outlook is poor without repair.

correlates.name: Cardiogenic shock
correlates.presentation: 64-year-old man 6 hours into a large anterior STEMI: confused, with cold, clammy gray skin, mottled knees and urine output 10 mL/h. BP 76/50 despite a 500 mL fluid bolus, HR 122, RR 30, SpO2 88%; JVP 10 cm; crackles over both lower lung halves; S3.
correlates.workup: Lactate 5.8, creatinine rising; echo: anterior and apical akinesis, EF 20% (over 40% of the LV lost), no new murmur, no effusion, normal RV; PA catheter: PCWP 28 mmHg, cardiac index 1.5 L/min/m2, high SVR.
correlates.management: Emergent revascularization of the culprit artery (PCI); norepinephrine for pressure plus dobutamine for contractility; mechanical support (intra-aortic balloon pump, Impella, ECMO) if needed; no beta blockers or nitrates while hypotensive.

correlates.name: Reinfarction after recent MI
correlates.presentation: 59-year-old man on day 5 after a STEMI treated with fibrinolysis alone (no stent): new crushing substernal pressure at rest for 40 minutes with sweating - not pleuritic, not positional - unrelieved by nitroglycerin. BP 132/84, HR 102, no new murmur, neck veins flat, lungs clear.
correlates.workup: ECG: new ST elevation in the original leads; troponin still high from the first infarct (it stays up 7-10 days), so it cannot answer the question; CK-MB, which had normalized by day 3, has risen again to 28 ng/mL.
correlates.management: Manage as a new ST-elevation event: aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitor, heparin and emergent angiography with PCI of the reoccluded artery; continue high-intensity statin and beta blocker.

correlates.name: Cyanide toxicity from nitroprusside
correlates.presentation: 62-year-old man with diabetes and CKD (creatinine 3.1) on day 2 of a continuous IV vasodilator infusion started for a BP of 200/100: now confused and short of breath, with flushed red skin. BP 118/70, HR 116, RR 30, SpO2 98% on room air, no cyanosis; then a seizure.
correlates.workup: pH 7.18, HCO3- 9, gap 28, lactate 11 mmol/L; PaO2 normal but central venous O2 saturation 88% (tissues cannot extract O2 - cytochrome c oxidase blocked); osmolar gap and ketones normal; thiocyanate level high.
correlates.management: Stop the infusion; 100% O2; IV hydroxocobalamin (binds the toxin to form cyanocobalamin, vitamin B12, excreted in urine) and/or sodium thiosulfate (sulfur donor); switch to a different IV antihypertensive.

correlates.name: Calcium channel blocker overdose
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old woman found drowsy 3 h after swallowing a handful of her husband's extended-release pills for BP and heart-rate control. HR 42, BP 70/40, RR 16, SpO2 97%; lungs clear, no wheeze; warm, dry skin. Fingerstick glucose 310; she does not have diabetes.
correlates.workup: ECG: sinus bradycardia with PR 280 ms sliding into a junctional rhythm, narrow QRS, normal QTc; glucose 310 mg/dL (insulin release from islet cells blocked); K+ 4.2; lactate 4; digoxin level undetectable.
correlates.management: IV fluids and atropine; IV Ca2+ (chloride or gluconate); high-dose insulin with dextrose; vasopressors; glucagon may help; pacing, lipid emulsion or ECMO if refractory; whole-bowel irrigation for extended-release pills.

correlates.name: Beta blocker overdose
correlates.presentation: 16-year-old girl brought in 2 h after swallowing a handful of her grandmother's blood-pressure pills; drowsy, wheezing and short of breath. HR 45, BP 90/60, RR 24, SpO2 94%; diffuse expiratory wheezes; normal pupils. Fingerstick glucose 55.
correlates.workup: ECG: sinus bradycardia at 45 with PR 240 ms (first-degree AV block) and a narrow QRS; glucose 55 mg/dL (hepatic glycogen breakdown blocked); K+ 5.0; digoxin level undetectable; acetaminophen and aspirin screens negative.
correlates.management: IV glucagon bolus then infusion (raises cAMP downstream of the blocked receptor); atropine, IV fluids and dextrose; high-dose insulin with dextrose and catecholamines if refractory; pacing; inhaled bronchodilator for the wheeze.

correlates.name: Reye syndrome
correlates.presentation: 7-year-old boy recovering from influenza who was given his grandfather's aspirin for fever. Five days later: relentless vomiting, then lethargy, combativeness and a seizure. Temp 37.4 C, HR 120; liver edge 3 cm below the costal margin; no jaundice, rash or neck stiffness.
correlates.workup: AST 420, ALT 380 U/L; ammonia 210 umol/L; PT prolonged; glucose 48; bilirubin normal; CSF: normal cells and protein, high opening pressure; liver biopsy: hepatocytes filled with tiny fat droplets, swollen mitochondria, no inflammation.
correlates.management: ICU supportive care: dextrose-containing fluids, lower intracranial pressure (head up, mannitol or hypertonic saline), vitamin K/plasma for the coagulopathy. Prevention: no aspirin for fever in children (Kawasaki disease is the exception).

correlates.name: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
correlates.presentation: 6-year-old girl whose parents are first cousins: nosebleeds lasting over an hour since infancy, gum bleeding with brushing, easy bruising and prolonged bleeding after a tooth extraction. No joint or muscle bleeds; normal growth; no enlarged liver or spleen.
correlates.workup: Platelets 290,000/uL, normal size on smear; PT and PTT normal; PFA closure time prolonged; no aggregation with ADP, collagen, epinephrine or thrombin but normal response to ristocetin; flow cytometry: absent GP IIb/IIIa (CD41/CD61).
correlates.management: Local measures and tranexamic acid for mucosal bleeds; platelet transfusion (HLA-matched when possible) or recombinant factor VIIa for serious bleeds or surgery; avoid aspirin and NSAIDs; iron for chronic losses.
